what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) analyze data structured as networks—friends on social media, molecules, roads. Real-time serving of GNNs has two problems: computing aggregations from neighbors and the explosion where each layer sees exponentially more neighbors. FLAG (an FPGA-based system) solves this by precomputing and compressing the neighborhood data offline using vector quantization (storing dense numbers as short lookup codes). The FPGA then does lightweight online aggregation with the compressed embeddings, eliminating repeated computation and meeting tight latency targets for services.
